subject: President Ali Bongo's New Year's address
called_fake_by: Political opponents, including former presidential rival Bruno Ben Moubamba
claim: Bongo had been out of public view for months while being treated abroad; Gabon's vice president described his illness as a stroke. When his New Year's Eve video showed him looking stiff and unnatural, opponents said it was a deepfake meant to hide his condition.
finding: Forensic analysis turned up no evidence of a deepfake, and the available tests favored authenticity. Experts suggested illness and makeup or cosmetic work as likelier explanations for how he looked. They stopped short of calling the question fully settled.
outcome: On January 7, 2019, soldiers briefly seized the state broadcaster in a coup attempt. They questioned Bongo's health and his fitness to govern and criticized the address. That is separate from the opponents' deepfake claim. The coup failed the same morning.

sources.title: The Bizarre and Terrifying Case of the "Deepfake" Video that Helped Bring an African Nation to the Brink
